desktop.pico_setup_menu.choose1.overview: Choose what you want to work on. Returning to Home keeps your open documents in memory; save them before switching the calculator off.

items.0: Go back to the calculator stack.
items.1: Open graphs, equation solving, calculus and the mathematical workbenches.
items.2: Work with X,Y tables or a notebook of expressions and notes.
items.3: Find RPL, Lua, CHIP-8 and sprite tools, or inspect stored variables.
items.4: Convert a measurement or an amount of money.
items.5: Save and load your work, or save and return to the loader.
items.6: Change display, calculation, clock and network settings.
items.7: Read help, find a command or view the credits.

desktop.pico_setup_menu.choose2.overview: Choose a mathematical tool. Answers stay in the tool until you explicitly copy or store them, so exploring does not clutter the stack.

items.0: Choose a graph type, edit formulas and plot them.
items.1: Solve an equation or system, or adjust parameters in a plot.
items.2: Open Calculus in X, Multivariable calculus, Symbolic algebra, or Value / approximation.
items.3: Keep a reusable formula with named inputs and optional units.
items.4: Choose Matrix workbench or Vector workbench.
items.5: Choose the financial calculator or the engineering RLC / RC-filter workbench.
items.6: Open guided normal, binomial and Poisson probability calculations and plots.
items.7: Open complex numbers or the applied-math tools: units, uncertainty, interpolation/fitting, discrete mathematics and signal analysis.

desktop.pico_setup_menu.choose3.overview: Tables and notebooks each have their own Files menu. Save the document there; saving the calculator session alone does not save it.

items.0: Enter paired data and explore statistics, regression or plots.
items.1: Keep calculations and notes in cells, then run them when ready.
items.2: Open the shared probability workbench for normal, binomial and Poisson calculations and plots.
items.3: Calculate confidence intervals, mean tests and fitted distributions from the current data table.
items.4: Interpolate current data or fit a nonlinear model with explicit starting guesses.
items.5: Analyze uniformly sampled Y data using FFTs and bounded filters.

desktop.pico_program_browser.choose1.overview: Choose the kind of program or drawing you want to use. RPL programs take arguments from the calculator stack and leave results there.

items.0: Find programs stored in HOME. F2 runs the selected body.
items.1: Open RPL source/binary files from /db48x/data.
items.2: Run a CHIP-8 ROM or edit and assemble its source.
items.3: Run or edit scripts from /db48x/lua.
items.4: Draw a colour sprite or a CHIP-8 mask.
items.5: Look through calculator variables without replacing them.
items.6: Try Lua a line at a time; its variables last until the console closes.

desktop.native_settings.choose1.overview: Most changes apply as soon as you choose them. Save the calculator session to keep calculator display and calculation settings after restart.

items.0: Choose the colours used throughout the interface.
items.1: Set angles and precision, or open the advanced calculator menus.
items.2: Choose the timezone used for displayed time.
items.3: Set up Wi-Fi and check its connection.
items.4: Check battery, memory and radio information.

desktop.native_settings.choose2.overview: Choose a palette that is comfortable on your display. Enter applies it immediately; save your calculator session to keep it after restart.

items.0: Light paper with dark text and blue controls.
items.1: Dark blue with cool text and mint results.
items.2: Black with warm amber text.
items.3: Dark green with mint text.
items.4: Warm paper with brown text.
items.5: Deep teal with pale cyan text.
items.6: Black and grey with white text.
items.7: Purple with pale lilac text.

desktop.native_settings.choose3.overview: Angle mode and precision also affect formulas and graphs. Displayed decimal places are a separate setting from calculation precision.

items.0: Choose degrees, radians, grads or multiples of pi. Choosing the active mode leaves it active.
items.1: Set significant calculation digits. For comparison, 3 Fix changes only displayed decimal places.
items.2: Open calculator soft menus. Tab selects a row; Ctrl+F5 reaches column six. Beep toggles; numeric settings need a stack value. Esc goes back.

desktop.native_settings.choose4.overview: Choose the angle unit for trigonometric calculations and graph formulas. This changes future evaluations, not results already calculated.

desktop.native_settings.choose5.overview: These pages report what the hardware can actually supply. An unavailable value is not a full battery or a successful network connection.

items.0: Read percentage and charging state from the keyboard controller.
items.1: See internal memory budgets and PSRAM status; both RAM types lose work at power-off.
items.2: Check the connection. F4 shows recent attempts and any pending startup retry.

desktop.native_help.choose1.overview: Choose a guide for the task you are doing. Lua and CHIP-8 start with a first program; their command details and Find are in the same section. About and credits are at the bottom.

items.0: Read the built-in guide; its last entry opens Command reference.
items.1: Insert a calculator command from the catalogue. Supply its arguments before running it.
items.2: Find the Ctrl shortcuts and menu keys.
items.3: Browse Lua language and PicoCalc API examples, including drawing, plots, keys and sound.
items.4: Learn CHIP-8 assembly, keypad mapping and profiles with short programs and expected results.
items.5: See the installed release and calculator credits.
items.6: Read the open-source acknowledgements and license information.

desktop.about_menu.choose1.overview: LumaRPL uses the DB48X engine with PicoCalc controls and tools. Credits name the people and open-source software that make it possible.

items.0: Check the installed release and calculator credits.
items.1: Read acknowledgements; full license texts are on SD under /db48x/licenses.

desktop.native_files.choose1.overview: A session contains stack, variables and settings. The other choices open the file menu for each document type, so you can save that work separately.

items.0: Save the current calculator session.
items.1: Load the saved session, replacing current calculator state.
items.2: Save or load equations and parameter definitions.
items.3: Open saved graph, path or differential-equation files.
items.4: Save or load a reusable form and its input values.
items.5: Save or load notebook expressions and notes; run again after loading.
items.6: Import or export an X,Y table as CSV.
items.7: Save and return to the loader. Cancel or a required save failure keeps LumaRPL open.

desktop.native_files.choose2.overview: Choose the kind of graph you saved. Loading checks the file first and asks before applying its stored angle mode.

items.0: Open the files menu for 2D function scenes.
items.1: Open saved parametric or polar paths.
items.2: Open saved differential-equation problems.

conversion_ui.pico_conversions_menu.choo.overview: Choose a physical-unit conversion or currency conversion. An answer reaches the calculator stack only when you choose Copy.

items.0: Set a value and compatible source/destination units.
items.1: Set Amount, From and To, then Convert. Refresh is on the same page.
items.2: Enter the Wi-Fi name and password used for time and rate updates.

conversion_ui.currency_menu.choose1.overview: Set Amount, From and To, then Convert. From/To changes save automatically. Manage rates / settings has import, manual rates and network/date options.

items.0: Convert using the active rates; the answer includes its observation date.
items.1: Enter an amount or scalar expression.
items.2: Choose the source currency, such as CAD. Esc keeps the previous choice.
items.3: Choose the destination currency. It is remembered automatically.
items.4: Exchange the two currencies without changing the amount.
items.5: Connect, get time, download and validate rates. New rates work immediately, then save to SD.
items.6: Open import, manual rates, cache saving, Wi-Fi and date options.
items.7: Read where rates come from and what their dates mean.

conversion_ui.currency_pick.choose1.overview: Choose a three-letter currency code with Enter. Left/Right changes pages; Esc keeps the old choice. This selects a currency without converting yet.

conversion_ui.unit_conversion_menu.choos.overview: Set the value and both units before converting. Units need compatible dimensions; absolute temperatures differ from temperature differences.

items.0: Show the converted answer. F1 on that answer copies it.
items.1: Enter a number, fraction or ordinary scalar expression.
items.2: Choose the unit of the value you are starting with.
items.3: Choose a compatible unit for the answer.
items.4: Exchange From and To without changing the number.
items.5: Read conversion examples and custom-unit syntax.

conversion_ui.conversion_pick_unit.choos.overview: Choose a quantity, then its unit. For example, a length must convert to another length, rather than to a mass or temperature.
Enter selects the unit shown above. The full name is available here even when the list shortens it. Esc leaves the previous unit selected.

conversion_ui.timezone_menu.choose1.overview: This changes displayed local time, not UTC or the date of exchange-rate observations. Toronto/Eastern follows daylight saving; fixed offsets do not.

conversion_ui.currency_options.choose1.overview: These choices apply to the next currency refresh. The clock needs actual current time; the observation date can be historical.

items.0: Use NTP, or enter actual current UTC if NTP is blocked.
items.1: Request latest observations or a historical date.
items.2: Choose the displayed local timezone.
items.3: Read how the clock and observation date work together.

conversion_ui.currency_options.choose2.overview: Automatic NTP obtains current UTC before HTTPS. For Manual UTC, enter actual current UTC time, not your local time or the historical rate date.

conversion_ui.currency_options.choose3.overview: Latest asks for the newest provider observations. A historical date can return an earlier business day; check the date shown with the answer.

conversion_ui.wifi_setup.choose1.overview: Use a 2.4 GHz WPA2 personal network. Saving credentials allows quiet clock updates at startup; currency Refresh explicitly gets time and rates.

items.0: Enter the exact network name.
items.1: Enter the network password; the dialog masks it.
items.2: Choose this only for a network with no password.
items.3: Keep credentials on SD for future starts. The password and backups are readable on the card.
items.4: Delete saved credentials and recovery copies.
items.5: Check the connection; F4 shows attempt details.
items.6: Read connection, retry and refresh guidance.
items.7: Choose the local timezone for displayed time.

desktop.pico_graph_menu.choose1.overview: Choose a plot type. The views share tracing, panning and zooming controls, but each type has its own formulas and saved documents.

items.0: Enter up to three functions in X.
items.1: Use X(T),Y(T), or a polar radius r(T).
items.2: Draw a surface in X,Y; arrows rotate it.
items.3: Solve a first-order initial-value problem and show its direction field.
items.4: Choose saved graph files by their type.
items.5: Move six points defining two lines and a circle.
items.6: Plot the intersection of up to three Y-versus-f(X) inequalities with strict/inclusive boundaries.
items.7: Plot an implicit equation such as X^2+Y^2=25, or contour levels of a scalar field, through Advanced studies.

desktop.multi_menu.choose1.overview: Enter expressions in X without Y=. Clear a formula to disable that curve. All enabled curves share one window and the same analysis tools.

items.0: Sample the enabled functions and open the graph.
items.1: Change Y1; try X^2.
items.2: Change Y2; try SIN(X) in radians.
items.3: Change Y3, or clear it to disable it.
items.4: Set ordered X and Y window bounds.
items.5: Choose different curve colours.

desktop.formula_entry.choose1.overview: Choose a function or symbol to insert at the cursor. Function templates include punctuation; fill in their arguments before plotting or calculating.

desktop.formula_entry.choose2.overview: Insert a larger template or apply calculus to the current expression. F3 checks syntax; F4 previews the mathematical layout.

desktop.analysis_number.choose1.overview: Analysis works on the selected function over a chosen interval. Numerical searches can miss narrow or tangent features; they do not prove all solutions.

items.0: Look for resolved zeros within the bounds.
items.1: Choose another curve and look for a crossing.
items.2: Estimate a minimum within the bounds.
items.3: Estimate a maximum within the bounds.
items.4: Estimate the derivative at a specified X.
items.5: Integrate with sign, so positive and negative parts can cancel.
items.6: Integrate the absolute function value.
items.7: Choose another curve and integrate their absolute difference.

desktop.analysis_number.choose2.overview: Choose the other enabled function for intersections or area between curves. The currently traced function remains the first one.

desktop.analysis_number.choose3.overview: Choose where to search or integrate. Bounds limit the calculation; they do not guarantee that every feature inside them will be resolved.

items.0: Use the two X positions marked in the plot.
items.1: Type the lower and upper X bounds.

desktop.plot_curves.choose1.overview: Return from these choices with Esc to keep tracing the same graph. Export needs a writable SD card and writes under /db48x/exports.

items.0: Open controls for this kind of plot.
items.1: Save a vector SVG of the graph.
items.2: Save sampled coordinates as CSV; these are points, not an exact formula.

desktop.plot_curves.choose2.overview: These controls change the differential-equation view. Editing the initial point resamples the solution; visibility changes keep the equation.

items.0: Show or hide the tangent at the trace point.
items.1: Change X0,Y0 and solve again.
items.2: Show or hide the direction-field arrows.
items.3: Show or hide the solution curve.

desktop.plot_curves.choose3.overview: Explore a parametric or polar path using T. Equal scaling gives both axes the same physical scale, so circles look round.

items.0: Show or hide the numerical tangent.
items.1: Move to a T value inside its bounds.
items.2: Give X and Y equal screen scale.

desktop.plot_curves.choose4.overview: These controls act on the selected 2D curve. In the graph itself, F4 switches pan/trace and +/- zooms. Esc returns to tracing.

items.0: Show or hide its tangent.
items.1: Mark this X as a bound; mark another to make an interval.
items.2: Remove the marked interval.
items.3: Type an X within the visible window.
items.4: Adjust the workbench parameters without overwriting shared variables.

desktop.surface_menu.choose1.overview: Enter an expression in X,Y without Z=. Arrows rotate the rendered surface, +/- zooms, and Esc stops sampling or returns.

items.0: Draw the surface using its current formula.
items.1: Change the expression in X,Y.
items.2: Use the saddle X^2-Y^2.
items.3: Use SIN(X^2+Y^2); radians gives the usual ripple.
items.4: Set the sampling bounds in X and Y.

desktop.calculus_menu.choose1.overview: Calculus uses X as its variable. Use radians with trigonometric expressions. Unsupported symbolic operations report an error rather than inventing a result.

items.0: Find the symbolic derivative.
items.1: Find an antiderivative; the arbitrary constant is implicit.
items.2: Estimate the derivative at a numerical X.
items.3: Calculate a numerical signed definite integral.
items.4: Calculate numerical area using absolute values.
items.5: Try a symbolic definite integral.

desktop.scene_menu.choose1.overview: Function scenes keep formulas and graph settings under /db48x/graphs. Loading validates the document before replacing the current scene.

items.0: Name and save this scene.
items.1: Choose a scene to load; Esc keeps the current one.

desktop.edit_file.choose1.overview: These tools edit the open source document. Saving is separate; failed saves and cancelled Save & run keep the source available.

items.0: Open the matching language reference. Returning preserves your source, selection and unsaved changes.
items.1: Browse complete examples and open one as a separate named document. Your original source and undo history stay intact.
items.3: Search for text.
items.4: Replace a match or all matches.
items.5: Jump to a source line.
items.6: Undo the last grouped edit.
items.7: Redo an undone edit.
items.9: Read shortcuts or the complete file path.
items.2: Choose a language command, inspect its template, then insert at the cursor or replace the selection. Ctrl+Z undoes this edit.

desktop.edit_file.choose2.overview: Replacement changes the open source and marks it unsaved. Esc cancels this choice without replacing text.

items.0: Replace the next match.
items.1: Replace all matches in the source.

desktop.development_files.actions.overview: Choose information about the selected CHIP-8 file or the interpreter behavior it needs. Changing a profile does not alter calculator mathematics.

items.0: Read the complete filename, path and type.
items.1: Choose the interpreter profile expected by the ROM.

desktop.development_files.choose1.overview: Use the compatibility profile the ROM was written for. CHIP-8 display pixels remain monochrome in every profile.

items.0: Use classic COSMAC VIP behavior.
items.1: Use CHIP-48 behavior from the HP48 lineage.
items.2: Use modern SUPER-CHIP behavior.
items.3: Use HP48 SUPER-CHIP behavior.

sprite.tools.overview: Colour mode keeps RGB332 pixels and transparency. CHIP-8 mode keeps a one-bit mask, with colour used only for preview. Save before replacing work.

items.0: Open a saved .sprite after checking unsaved work.
items.1: Start a fresh colour drawing.
items.2: Convert to a one-bit mask; a populated colour drawing asks first.
items.3: Switch to full colour drawing.
items.4: Clear pixels after confirmation.
items.5: Export opaque pixels as set bits and transparent pixels as clear bits.
items.6: Read painting, saving and Lua drawing instructions.

workbench_ui.pico_workbench_menu.choose1.overview: Keep equations and parameters together without changing shared calculator variables. Save the workbench separately when you want it after restart.

items.0: Work with one equation in X.
items.1: Solve two or three equations together.
items.2: Plot with adjustable A,B,C.
items.3: Save or load a workbench.
items.4: Read solver and parameter controls.

workbench_ui.workbench_single.choose1.overview: A local solve starts from your guess; an interval search examines a bounded region. Symbolic isolation is a separate action and can be unsupported.

items.0: Edit the equation or residual expression.
items.1: Set the starting guess for X.
items.2: Find one solution from that guess.
items.3: Search between two bounds.
items.4: Try to isolate X symbolically.
items.5: Plot the equation residual.

workbench_ui.workbench_system.choose1.overview: Use X,Y for two equations or X,Y,Z for three. Each unknown needs a guess; singular or inconsistent systems may not converge.

items.0: Choose two or three unknowns.
items.1: Edit the first equation.
items.2: Edit the second equation.
items.3: Edit the third equation in a three-variable system.
items.4: Set the initial guesses.
items.5: Solve and inspect each residual.

workbench_ui.workbench_system.choose2.overview: Choose two unknowns X,Y or three unknowns X,Y,Z. Then enter the matching equations and one starting guess for each variable.

workbench_ui.workbench_parameters.choose.overview: The workbench owns A,B,C and their bounds. Sliders change these local values; Store parameters is the explicit way to update shared variables.

items.0: Open the parameter plot and adjust A,B,C in its F3 controls.
items.1: Change the expression in X,A,B,C.
items.2: Set A and its slider bounds and step.
items.3: Set B and its slider bounds and step.
items.4: Set C and its slider bounds and step.
items.5: Set the X,Y window bounds.
items.6: Copy one chosen parameter into its shared calculator variable.

workbench_ui.workbench_parameters.choose.overview: Choose which local parameter to store in the matching calculator variable A, B or C. This is the explicit step that changes a shared variable.

workbench_ui.workbench_use.choose1.overview: Viewing a result leaves your stack and variables alone. Choose how you want to use it, or go back without applying it.

items.1: Copy the result to the stack.
items.2: Store the solved value or values in calculator variables.

workbench_ui.workbench_use.choose2.overview: Choose the result you want to copy. The solver results remain available here; selecting one is the explicit stack-copy action.

workbench_ui.workbench_saved.choose1.overview: Workbench files keep equations, guesses, parameters, angle mode and graph settings. Results are temporary and are recalculated after loading.

items.0: Save this workbench under /db48x/workbenches.
items.1: Load a workbench after validation; protect unsaved changes first.

path_ui.pico_path_menu.choose1.overview: Parametric plots use X(T),Y(T); polar plots use r(T). T follows the calculator angle mode, and the same graph controls work in both modes.

items.0: Draw the current path.
items.1: Choose parametric or polar mode.
items.2: Edit X(T), or r(T) in polar mode.
items.3: Edit Y(T) when using parametric mode.
items.4: Set the first and last T.
items.5: Set the graph window.
items.6: Choose a worked example or read Help.
items.7: Save or load a .path file.

path_ui.pico_path_menu.choose2.overview: Parametric mode uses two expressions in T. Polar mode uses a radius expression in T. The current angle mode determines the angular unit.

path_ui.pico_path_menu.choose3.overview: These examples replace the current path and use radians. Save important changes before choosing one; replacement asks first.

path_ui.path_files.choose1.overview: Path files keep expressions, T bounds, angle mode and window under /db48x/paths. Loading asks before applying the saved angle mode.

items.0: Save the current path.
items.1: Choose and load a path file.

ode_ui.pico_ode_menu.choose1.overview: Enter a first-order slope expression in X,Y and an initial point. The solution is numerical and may stop at a domain error or its work budget.

items.0: Draw the solution and direction field.
items.1: Edit the slope expression without dy/dX=.
items.2: Set the initial X0,Y0.
items.3: Set the visible window.
items.4: Start from an example.
items.5: Save or load an equation file.
items.6: Read the method, controls and limitations.
items.7: Solve coupled first-order systems or second-order initial-value problems, with phase portraits and tables.

ode_ui.pico_ode_menu.choose2.overview: Choose an example differential equation. The expression and initial conditions are replaced so you can explore a complete problem.

ode_ui.ode_files.choose1.overview: Equation files under /db48x/odes keep the slope, initial point and graph settings. A load is checked before it replaces current work.

items.0: Save this differential-equation problem.
items.1: Load a saved problem and confirm its angle mode.

form_ui.pico_forms_menu.choose1.overview: A form keeps a reusable formula and named inputs. Calculate when ready; saving the form is separate from saving the calculator session.

items.0: Give the form a title.
items.1: Change the formula using its input names.
items.2: Add or edit named inputs, values and units.
items.3: Calculate with the current inputs.
items.4: Vary one input along a graph.
items.5: Save or load this form.
items.6: Choose a worked example or read Help.
items.7: Choose optional result units with compatible dimensions.

form_ui.form_field_edit.choose1.overview: Edit the input definition. Names must match the formula, and a later input may use the value of an earlier one.

items.0: Change the value or expression.
items.1: Rename this input; update its name in the formula too.
items.2: Delete this input and check the formula afterward.
items.3: Choose its optional declared unit.

form_ui.form_fields.choose1.overview: Choose an existing input to edit it, or add one while fewer than six exist. Use the same names in the formula and input definitions.

form_ui.form_graph.choose1.overview: Choose the input to vary along the horizontal axis. Other definitions stay in place; shared calculator variables are not overwritten.

form_ui.form_files.choose1.overview: Saved forms keep the formula, named inputs, units and values under /db48x/forms. A failed load leaves the current form in place.

items.0: Save this form.
items.1: Open a saved form after validation.

form_ui.pico_forms_menu.choose2.overview: Choose a formula to start from. Save current changes before replacing the form, especially if you want to keep its input values.

notebook_ui.pico_notebooks_menu.choose1.overview: A notebook holds expressions and notes. Nothing runs while editing or loading; choose Run when you want results refreshed.

items.0: Choose a cell.
items.1: Run cells from the start in order.
items.2: Add a cell, up to twelve.
items.3: Save or load expressions and notes.
items.4: Change the notebook title.
items.5: Replace current content with demo cells.
items.6: Read cell references and saving behavior.

notebook_ui.notebook_cells.choose1.overview: Open a cell to edit, run through it, inspect it or delete it. Merely selecting a cell does not evaluate the notebook.

notebook_ui.notebook_cell.choose1.overview: Run through starts at cell one and stops here. Moving or deleting cells changes their numbers, so check later R1..R12 references afterward.

items.0: Edit this expression.
items.1: Edit its note without executing anything.
items.2: Read the note and most recent result.
items.3: Run from cell one through this cell.
items.4: Move the cell one place earlier.
items.5: Delete this cell.

notebook_ui.notebook_files.choose1.overview: Notebook files keep expressions and notes under /db48x/notebooks. Results are refreshed by an explicit Run after loading.

items.0: Save this notebook.
items.1: Load a saved notebook after checking unsaved changes.

data_ui.pico_data_menu.choose1.overview: Enter paired X,Y observations, then inspect statistics, fit a model or plot them. Use Files to save or import a CSV table.

items.0: Edit the table: F1 adds, F2 deletes, F3 shows statistics and F4 plots.
items.1: Read column statistics.
items.2: Choose a regression model.
items.3: Plot observations and the fitted curve.
items.4: Plot Y minus its fitted value.
items.5: Import or export paired CSV data.
items.6: Replace the table with demo data after confirmation.

data_ui.data_summary.choose1.overview: These statistics use the current table. Choose a column and measure when you want to copy a value to the calculator stack.

data_ui.data_summary.choose2.overview: Choose whether the statistic should use the X column or Y column. This does not change or rearrange the table.

data_ui.data_summary.choose3.overview: Choose a statistic to copy from the selected column. Sample variance and deviation need at least two observations.

items.0: Copy the minimum.
items.1: Copy the maximum.
items.2: Copy the mean.
items.3: Copy the median.
items.4: Copy the total.
items.5: Copy population variance, using n.
items.6: Copy sample variance, using n-1.
items.7: Copy sample standard deviation.

data_ui.data_regression.choose1.overview: Choose a least-squares model suited to your data. Logarithmic transformations require positive values in the affected columns.

items.0: Fit Y=a+bX.
items.1: Fit Y=a+b*ln(X), requiring X>0.
items.2: Fit Y=a*exp(bX), requiring Y>0.
items.3: Fit Y=a*X^b, requiring X,Y>0.

data_ui.data_regression.choose2.overview: Choose how to use the fitted result. Using Y1 replaces the 2D curve set; copying adds the selected object to the stack.

items.0: Copy coefficient a.
items.1: Copy coefficient b.
items.2: Copy the expression in X.
items.3: Use the fit as Y1 in a new active curve set.
items.4: Save the fit as a graph scene.
items.5: Copy correlation where defined; nonlinear fits use transformed data.
items.6: Copy squared correlation where defined.

data_ui.data_files.choose1.overview: CSV tables live under /db48x/data. Imports are checked before replacing the current paired table; failed loading keeps it.

items.0: Save the table as CSV.
items.1: Import a supported two-column CSV file.

conversion_ui.currency_tools.overview: Manage the rates used by Currency conversion. Return with F5 to see Amount, From and To; imported/manual rates need a cache save for restart.

items.0: Import a validated .rates table.
items.1: Edit a rate quoted as units per EUR and its date.
items.2: Save the active table for offline use after restart.
items.3: Set up the network name and password.
items.4: Choose time, observation-date and timezone options.

editor.help_details.overview: Read the editor controls or the complete source-file path. Returning keeps the source, cursor and unsaved state unchanged.

items.0: Read the source-editor shortcuts.
items.1: Read the entire file path.

math.matrix.menu.overview: Work on A and B without changing the calculator stack. Results offer Copy, and matrix results can be used as A for another operation.

items.0: Edit matrix A.
items.1: Set up B and combine it with A.
items.2: Use determinant, inverse, transpose or solving.
items.3: Save/load A or import the top stack matrix.
items.4: Read the matrix controls and examples.
items.5: Keep matrices in named HOME variables.
items.6: Use powers, echelon forms, rank and system classification.

math.finance.menu.overview: Rates for loans are nominal annual percentages divided by periods/year. Cash-flow discount rates are per interval. Read Help before comparing a lender quote.

items.0: Set principal, rates, periods, timing and other inputs.
items.1: Find the payment magnitude that amortizes the loan.
items.2: Calculate growth, savings, rate or term.
items.3: Read balance, principal and interest after payments.
items.4: Enter signed cash flows and calculate NPV/IRR.
items.5: Save inputs and cash flows.
items.6: Load a finance file after validation.
items.7: Read examples and finance conventions.

math.finance.inputs.overview: Enter percentages as 5 for 5%, not 0.05. Periods are counts, not years. Changing these fields leaves engine TVM variables alone.

items.0: Set loan principal or initial investment.
items.1: Set nominal annual interest percentage.
items.2: Set the total count of periods, from 1 to 100000.
items.3: Set periods per year, from 1 to 366; monthly is 12.
items.4: Choose beginning or end payment/deposit timing.
items.5: Set the discount percentage per cash-flow interval.
items.6: Set the payment used for rate/term solving.
items.7: Set the deposit used for regular savings.

math.finance.cashmenu.overview: CF0 happens now. Later flows are equally spaced. Negative amounts are outflows and positive amounts are inflows; discount/IRR percentages are per interval.

items.0: Edit the signed amounts.
items.1: Set the count including CF0, from 1 to 17.
items.2: Calculate net present value.
items.3: Set the discount percentage per interval.
items.4: Search for IRR within its configured interval.
items.5: Set -100 < first < last <= 10000 percent.

math.matrix.files.overview: Matrix files keep dimensions and cell expressions under /db48x/matrices. Loading validates the complete file before replacing the working grid.

items.0: Save this matrix under a chosen name.
items.1: Open a .matrix file.
items.2: Read level 1 without consuming it. The matrix must fit 6x6 and 31-byte cells.

math.matrix.arithmetic.overview: A and B are separate working matrices. Calculations keep both inputs; Copy or Use in A applies a result explicitly.

items.0: Edit B without changing A.
items.1: Save/load B or import a stack matrix into it.
items.2: Add equal-sized matrices.
items.3: Subtract B from A; sizes must match.
items.4: Multiply A by B; columns(A)=rows(B).
items.5: Calculate A*inverse(B); B must be square and invertible.
items.6: Scale A, divide it by a nonzero scalar or negate it.
items.7: Exchange A and B, keeping both; they become unsaved.

math.matrix.scalar.overview: Enter an ordinary real expression such as 1/3 for the scalar. The answer does not replace A unless you choose Use in A.

items.0: Multiply every entry by k.
items.1: Divide every entry by nonzero k.
items.2: Change the sign of every entry.

math.matrix.operations.overview: These operations use matrix A. A matrix result can become A for chaining; copying a result to the calculator stack is always explicit.

items.0: Find the determinant of square A.
items.1: Find the inverse of square, nonsingular A.
items.2: Exchange rows and columns.
items.3: Solve the augmented matrix with b last, with b in the last column.
items.4: Find characteristic roots of a 2x2 matrix.

math.matrix.register_actions.overview: A register is a named HOME variable. Loading a register keeps the stored matrix and calculator stack intact; overwriting a variable asks first.

items.0: Read or copy the selected matrix.
items.1: Store B under a name.
items.2: Read register controls and persistence.

math.matrix.reduction.overview: Reduction keeps A unchanged until you apply the result. For system classification, the last column is the right-hand side.

items.0: Raise A to an integer power from -32 to 32; negative powers need an inverse.
items.1: Find row echelon form.
items.2: Find reduced row echelon form.
items.3: Find rank from the reduced rows.
items.4: Compare coefficient/augmented ranks to classify solutions.

math.complex.menu.overview: Z and W can each be rectangular or polar. The phase unit belongs to this workbench, so calculator angle settings are restored after calculations.

items.0: Enter both parts of Z.
items.1: Enter both parts of W.
items.2: Convert Z, inspect it or find its roots.
items.3: Combine Z with W.
items.4: Choose degrees or radians for local phase inputs.
items.5: Save or load Z, W and phase unit.
items.6: Read complex examples and conventions.

math.complex.form.overview: Choose rectangular or polar entry. Both component prompts must succeed before the old value is replaced; Esc keeps it.

items.0: Enter the real part, then imaginary part.
items.1: Enter a nonnegative magnitude, then phase.

math.complex.operations.overview: These choices use Z. Phase uses the local angle unit; zero has no defined phase. Roots include multiplicities.

items.0: Show rectangular Z.
items.1: Show polar Z.
items.2: Find its magnitude.
items.3: Find the phase of nonzero Z.
items.4: Conjugate Z.
items.5: Find all n-th roots for n from 2 to 16.

math.complex.arithmetic.overview: These operations retain Z and W. Fractions stay exact where supported; dividing by zero reports an error without changing inputs.

items.0: Add Z and W.
items.1: Subtract W from Z.
items.2: Multiply Z by W.
items.3: Divide Z by nonzero W.

math.complex.files.overview: Files under /db48x/complex keep both values, their entry forms and phase unit. Loading checks the file and protects unsaved work first.

items.0: Save this complex workbench.
items.1: Load a saved workbench, recovering a backup where possible.

math.geometry.menu.overview: Six points define infinite lines AB/CD and a circle centred at E through F. Explore them in the shared graph or edit their coordinates.

items.0: Open the graph and move points.
items.1: Choose a point to edit numerically.
items.2: Read lengths, radius and intersections.
items.3: Show or hide construction layers.
items.4: Restore the demo after checking unsaved changes.
items.5: Save or load a construction.
items.6: Read movement and measurement guidance.
items.7: Declare coordinate units, rescale existing coordinates/window into compatible units, or explicitly remove units while retaining magnitudes. New coordinate entries accept quantities.

math.geometry.points.overview: A/B define the first line and C/D the second. E is the circle centre; F lies on its circumference. Changing a point updates the construction.

items.0: Change point A.
items.1: Change point B.
items.2: Change point C.
items.3: Change point D.
items.4: Move the circle centre E.
items.5: Move F to change the circle radius.

math.geometry.layers.overview: Visibility changes only what is drawn. All six points keep their coordinates and remain available for selection and editing.

items.0: Show or hide infinite line AB.
items.1: Show or hide infinite line CD.
items.2: Show or hide the circle through F, centred at E.

math.geometry.files.overview: Geometry files retain the six points, visible layers, selected point and window. Save before restart to keep changes.

items.0: Save under /db48x/geometry.
items.1: Load a checked construction or recover its valid backup.

math.geometry.explore.overview: In move mode, arrows change the selected point by one percent of the visible span. Esc returns to tracing; pan and zoom remain available.

items.0: Start moving the selected point.
items.1: Type its X and Y coordinates.
items.2: Read the construction measurements.

math.finance.more.overview: Growth uses nominal annual rate divided by periods/year. Rate/term solving uses Payment, while regular-deposit savings uses Deposit.

items.0: Calculate future value without added deposits.
items.1: Include regular deposits using the selected timing.
items.2: Solve nominal annual interest from principal, payment and term.
items.3: Solve a possibly fractional payment count.

form_ui.examples_help.overview: Start from a supplied example or read the tool instructions. Reading Help leaves the document alone; choosing an example can replace it.

items.0: Choose an example after protecting current changes.
items.1: Read controls, examples and limits.

path_ui.examples_help.overview: Start from a supplied example or read the tool instructions. Reading Help leaves the document alone; choosing an example can replace it.

items.0: Choose an example after protecting current changes.
items.1: Read controls, examples and limits.

math.finance.flows.overview: Edit the amount for the selected cash-flow period. CF0 is now; later periods are equally spaced. The parent menu changes how many flows are included.

items.0: Set the signed amount for CF0.
items.1: Set the signed amount for CF1.
items.2: Set the signed amount for CF2.

reference.topics.overview: Choose a guide topic and read it with arrows. F5 returns here. Command reference opens the same style of reader, with browsing and Find.

items.0: Get started with calculations, tools and saving.
items.1: Find your way around lists and calculator soft menus.
items.2: Use the stack, store a value and run a small program.
items.3: Enter a graph, explore it and use calculus.
items.4: Solve equations and adjust plot parameters.
items.5: Work with tables, reusable forms and notebooks.
items.6: Run programs, edit source and draw sprites.
items.7: Convert units and currencies, online or offline.
items.8: Save work, recover from errors and return to the loader.
items.9: Connect Wi-Fi and choose clock/rate dates.
items.10: Choose colours, mathematical fonts and calculator settings.
items.11: Browse or find a command, then read its page. Arrows scroll or page; F5 returns to the list.

reference.subjects.overview: Find a command by name or browse a subject. Each entry opens a normal help page; F5 brings you back to the same list.

editor.examples.overview: Choose an example to read its source and expected result. Open creates a separate unsaved document; returning restores your original editor.

math.lab.files.overview: Save or load the inputs for all five math workbenches together. The workbench angle mode is scoped to these tools; your calculator angle setting is restored when you leave.

items.0: Save all five workbenches, their formulas, inputs, bounds and angle mode in one .mathlab file.
items.1: Load a validated .mathlab document; unsaved replacements require confirmation. A valid backup can recover a failed replacement.
items.2: Choose the saved workbench angle mode.
items.3: Read help and a worked example for the current workbench.

math.lab.angle.overview: Choose the angle mode used by formulas in these workbenches. Normal/binomial/Poisson probabilities and vector angles labelled degrees are independent of this choice.

math.lab.vector_plane.overview: Choose which two coordinates to draw. The native path traces A and B from the origin; 3D vectors are shown as projections, not a perspective 3D arrow view.

math.lab.vectors.overview: Enter real scalar expressions for A and B, then choose a calculation or plot. The inputs remain available when you return. Results are copied to the stack only when you choose Copy.

math.lab.vector_dimension.overview: Choose two or three components. The hidden third components are retained when you switch to 2D.

math.lab.vector_operations.overview: Choose an operation on the current A and B. The 2D cross result is its signed Z component. Projection requires nonzero B; an angle requires both vectors to be nonzero.

math.lab.probability.overview: Choose a distribution and parameters, then enter a point, an interval or a percentile probability. Calculate gives density, mass, cumulative/tail probability, interval probability or an inverse lookup.

math.lab.distribution.overview: Normal uses mean and standard deviation. Binomial uses integer trials n and success probability p. Poisson uses its mean lambda. Choosing a distribution starts it with valid default parameters.

items.3: Declare measurement units for the normal distribution. Mean, SD, point and interval entries accept compatible quantities; CDF probabilities remain dimensionless.

math.lab.probability_operations.overview: Use the stored point/interval/percentile. Density is not point probability. Discrete intervals include both integer endpoints. Inverse CDF returns the smallest integer meeting the cumulative probability.

items.5: Use data-table observations for inference or fit a normal distribution; returning keeps this calculation menu open.

math.lab.regions.overview: Each enabled boundary compares Y with a function of X. The shaded area satisfies all enabled conditions together. Strict inequalities use dashed boundary lines. Missing-domain columns are not shaded.

math.lab.relation.overview: Choose above/below and whether equality is included, then edit f(X). Disabled boundaries retain their formulas for later use.

math.lab.multivariable.overview: F and G are formulas in X and Y. Use Calculate for derivatives, gradient, Jacobian, Hessian, values and a rectangular numerical double integral. Plot F or a numerical tangent plane using the native surface view.

math.lab.multivariable_operations.overview: Gradient order is X,Y. Jacobian rows are F,G and columns X,Y. Hessian rows/columns are X,Y. The double integral uses the stored increasing X/Y bounds and bounded refinement; domain errors or failed convergence are reported.

math.lab.algebra.overview: Transform an expression with upstream DB48X rules. Replacement and variable are used by Substitute. Viewing results preserves the expression; Use result explicitly replaces it after confirmation.

math.lab.variable.overview: Choose the symbol to replace. Substitute changes that symbol in the expression without storing a calculator variable.

math.lab.algebra_operations.overview: Simplify, Expand, Collect, Partial fractions and Substitute use DB48X. Collect can factor supported patterns; unsupported forms are retained or reported by the engine without a numerical fallback.

math.lab.calculus_route.overview: Choose one-variable calculus, two-variable calculus, symbolic algebra or the existing stack value/approximation view.

items.4: Enter polynomial coefficients, solve for roots, evaluate, multiply, divide and plot.

math.lab.matrix_route.overview: Use the matrix grid for matrix arithmetic and linear algebra. Use the vector workbench for 2D/3D real vectors, projection, angle and endpoint distance.

math.lab.vector_arithmetic.overview: Add/subtract A and B, scale A with the stored real k, divide A by nonzero k, or normalize nonzero A. Operations use DB48X arithmetic; the input vectors remain unchanged.

items.5: Edit the scale k as a real expression, such as 2 or 1/3.

math.lab.bounds.overview: The integration rectangle and surface display window are separate. Enter increasing X and Y bounds. Changing either leaves the other unchanged.

items.0: Set the rectangle used by the numerical double integral.
items.1: Set X and Y limits for Plot F and the tangent-plane view.

advanced.files.overview: Files / help. Use arrows / Enter or visible row numbers. F5 / Esc goes back one level.

items.0: Save all advanced workbench inputs together in a named .advanced file. Results are not saved.
items.1: Load a checked document; unsaved inputs require confirmation before replacement.
items.2: Read worked examples and the assumptions behind the calculations.

advanced.polynomial.overview: Guided polynomials. Use arrows / Enter or visible row numbers. F5 / Esc goes back one level.

items.0: Enter degree 1–8 and real coefficients from the highest power down to the constant. A zero leading coefficient is rejected.
items.1: Enter polynomial B for multiplication and division. This does not replace A.
items.2: Solve, evaluate, multiply or divide. The calculation menu stays open when you close a result.
items.3: Plot A with the native graph controls. Long expressions may exceed the graph editor limit.
items.4: Save or load inputs, or read the polynomial guide.
items.5: Declare X and output units for A and B. Bare coefficients are magnitudes in the implied output/X^power units.

advanced.polynomial_operations.overview: Polynomial calculations. Use arrows / Enter or visible row numbers. F5 / Esc goes back one level.

items.0: View the expression represented by A.
items.1: Find real and complex roots through DB48X. Repeated roots appear repeatedly; numerical roots can be approximate.
items.2: Enter a real X and evaluate A using the engine.
items.3: Multiply A and B, preserving the input coefficients.
items.4: Return the polynomial quotient of A divided by B. Use Remainder separately for the remaining term.
items.5: Return the remainder after polynomial division of A by B.

advanced.ode.overview: Systems / second-order ODE. Use arrows / Enter or visible row numbers. F5 / Esc goes back one level.

items.0: Choose a coupled system or a second-order equation. Both use Y and Z as dependent variables.
items.1: Coupled mode uses Y'=F(X,Y,Z), Z'=G(X,Y,Z). Second order uses Y'=Z and Z'=G.
items.2: Set initial X,Y,Z and a distinct final X. In second-order mode, initial Z is the initial derivative.
items.3: Solve with bounded adaptive RK4 refinement, then plot Y and Z against X.
items.4: Plot Y horizontally and Z vertically. In second-order mode this is position versus derivative.
items.5: Read 21 rows from the 201-point solution. Values are numerical estimates.
items.6: Save the equations and initial conditions or read the guide.
items.7: Declare X,Y,Z units. Right-hand sides must have the corresponding derivative dimensions. Second-order Z means Y'.

advanced.ode_mode.overview: Equation mode. Use arrows / Enter or visible row numbers. F5 / Esc goes back one level.

items.0: Enter two first-order right-hand sides in X,Y,Z.
items.1: Enter Y''=G(X,Y,Z), where Z stands for Y'.

advanced.engineering.overview: Engineering: RLC / RC filters. Use arrows / Enter or visible row numbers. F5 / Esc goes back one level.

items.0: Enter ohms, henries, farads and hertz. For a microfarad enter 1e-6.
items.1: Compute ideal series and parallel RLC complex impedance.
items.2: Calculate ideal unloaded RC low-pass and high-pass gain and phase. Inductance is not used here.
items.3: Plot both RC filters in dB against log10(frequency in Hz).
items.4: Plot filter phase in degrees against log10(frequency in Hz).
items.5: Choose increasing positive frequencies in hertz for the sweep.
items.6: Save circuit inputs or read the guide.

advanced.statistics.overview: Data inference / distributions. Use arrows / Enter or visible row numbers. F5 / Esc goes back one level.

items.0: Choose X, Y or paired X-Y differences from the current data table.
items.1: Set confidence as a fraction, the null mean and the null proportion.
items.2: Use sample standard deviation and Student t to estimate the population mean.
items.3: Calculate a two-sided one-sample Student t p-value. Paired differences give a paired t test.
items.4: Explicitly set the Probability normal distribution to the sample mean and sample standard deviation. This is a fit, not a normality test.
items.5: Enter successes and trials for a Wilson interval and approximate two-sided score test. Small expected counts need an exact method.
items.6: Save inference settings or read assumptions and examples.

advanced.sample.overview: Select data sample. Use arrows / Enter or visible row numbers. F5 / Esc goes back one level.

items.0: Use the X observations in the current table.
items.1: Use the Y observations in the current table.
items.2: Subtract each row's Y from X. Rows are matched pairs; pairs must be independent.

advanced.finance_route.overview: Finance / engineering. Use arrows / Enter or visible row numbers. F5 / Esc goes back one level.

items.0: Open the existing financial calculator.
items.1: Open ideal RLC impedance and RC filter responses, including Bode plots.

science.route.overview: More mathematics. Arrows/Enter choose; F5/Esc returns one level.

items.0: Open the existing complex-number workbench.
items.1: Evaluate expressions with physical units and convert results.
items.2: Propagate independent standard uncertainties through a formula.
items.3: Interpolate between observations or fit a nonlinear model.
items.4: Work with exact integers and bounded recurrence tables.
items.5: Analyze uniformly sampled Y data with FFTs and filters.
items.6: Open the consolidated advanced studies: implicit graphs, linear algebra, calculus, statistics, signals and connected documents.

science.files.overview: Files / help. Arrows/Enter choose; F5/Esc returns one level.

items.0: Save all applied-math settings in one checked .science file; data tables are saved separately as CSV.
items.1: Load a checked file; replacing unsaved settings needs confirmation.
items.2: Read worked examples, units and numerical limits for this tool.

science.data_units.overview: Data units. Arrows/Enter choose; F5/Esc returns one level.

items.0: Declare the units represented by the current CSV X magnitudes. This labels the numbers, not a conversion of the table.
items.1: Declare Y magnitude units for interpolation, signal amplitude and data inference. Save declarations in a .science document.

science.units.overview: Units and dimensions. Arrows/Enter choose; F5/Esc returns one level.

items.0: Enter an expression such as (12_V)/(4_ohm) or (2_m)+(30_cm).
items.1: Choose desired result units, such as A or cm. Empty retains the result units.
items.2: Evaluate with DB48X dimensional checking. F1 Copy explicitly adds the result to the stack.
items.3: Use the existing six-input formula forms, with units declared for each input and output.
items.4: Open the existing unit conversion tool, including compound units.
items.5: Declare units for numerical data columns. Bare CSV values are interpreted in these units.
items.6: Save inputs or read the guide.

science.uncertainty.overview: Measurement uncertainty. Arrows/Enter choose; F5/Esc returns one level.

items.0: Enter a smooth expression in independent measurements A, B and C. Trigonometric functions use radians.
items.1: Enter A, its nonnegative standard uncertainty and optional unit declaration.
items.2: Enter B, its nonnegative standard uncertainty and optional unit declaration.
items.3: Enter C and its uncertainty. Use zero uncertainty for a fixed input.
items.4: Choose compatible output units, or leave empty to infer them.
items.5: Combine first-order independent contributions in quadrature. This is not a confidence interval or correlated-error calculation.
items.6: Save measurements and formula, or read assumptions and examples.

science.fitting.overview: Interpolation / curve fitting. Arrows/Enter choose; F5/Esc returns one level.

items.0: Toggle linear or shape-preserving cubic interpolation.
items.1: Evaluate inside the sampled range. X must be strictly increasing without duplicates; no extrapolation is performed.
items.2: Plot interpolated values and original observations through the native engine.
items.3: Enter a numerical F(X,A,B,C) model and three starting guesses. Coefficients refer to declared X,Y magnitudes.
items.4: Run bounded unweighted local least squares. A singular model or failed convergence is reported; guesses are not silently replaced.
items.5: Create samples of 2*EXP(0.5*X)+1 after confirming replacement of the current data table.
items.6: Declare units represented by the X,Y magnitudes.
items.7: Save model/guesses/settings; save the source table separately as CSV.

science.fit_actions.overview: Converged nonlinear fit. Arrows/Enter choose; F5/Esc returns one level.

items.0: Read A,B,C and residual sum of squares. Copy adds a coefficient vector explicitly.
items.1: Plot the fitted model with the original observations and interpolation.
items.2: Plot observed Y minus fitted Y at each source X.
items.3: Explicitly adopt the converged values as the next starting guesses.

science.discrete.overview: Discrete mathematics. Arrows/Enter choose; F5/Esc returns one level.

items.0: Enter unsigned decimal integers up to 1e12. Fractional values are rejected rather than rounded.
items.1: Choose exact integer operations. Each operation returns to this submenu.
items.2: Enter F(N,U), initial U at N=0 and a row count up to 128.
items.3: Evaluate numerical recurrence values with cancellation and range checks. Installing the generated table needs confirmation.
items.4: Save integer and recurrence inputs, or read the guide.

science.integer_operations.overview: Exact integer calculations. Arrows/Enter choose; F5/Esc returns one level.

items.0: Euclidean greatest common divisor of A and B. GCD(0,0)=0.
items.1: Exact least common multiple; a zero operand gives zero.
items.2: Return A modulo positive B.
items.3: Compute A^B modulo positive M without constructing A^B.
items.4: Factor A from 2 through 1e9 by interruptible bounded trial division. Repeated factors are retained.
items.5: Exact A choose B, requiring 0<=B<=A<=1000.
items.6: Exact ordered selections A pick B, requiring 0<=B<=A<=1000.

science.sequence_actions.overview: Generated sequence. Arrows/Enter choose; F5/Esc returns one level.

items.0: Read the recurrence rows. A truncation notice directs you to CSV if the reader buffer fills.
items.1: Plot N against U(N) using the native graph engine.
items.2: Export every generated row without replacing the current table.
items.3: Confirm replacement of the current X,Y table with the generated sequence.

science.spectrum.overview: One-sided FFT. Arrows/Enter choose; F5/Esc returns one level.

items.0: Plot one-sided peak amplitudes with coherent-window-gain correction. Joined bins are a display interpolation.
items.1: Plot wrapped phase in degrees; very weak bins are omitted.
items.2: Read bin frequencies in hertz and peak amplitudes in declared Y units.
items.3: Export frequency/amplitude rows. Phase is not included in this CSV.

science.signal_settings.overview: FFT settings. Arrows/Enter choose; F5/Esc returns one level.

items.0: Set the uniform sample rate in hertz; unit quantities such as 2_kHz are accepted.
items.1: Cycle rectangular, Hann and Hamming windows.
items.2: Toggle mean removal before windowing. DC is removed when enabled.

science.filter.overview: Time-domain filters. Arrows/Enter choose; F5/Esc returns one level.

items.0: Cycle centered moving average, one-pole low-pass and one-pole high-pass.
items.1: Set cutoff below Nyquist and an odd average span from 3 through 31.
items.2: Filter a snapshot of Y. Source data remain unchanged until explicit replacement.

science.filter_actions.overview: Filtered data. Arrows/Enter choose; F5/Esc returns one level.

items.0: Plot filtered Y at the original X coordinates.
items.1: Export filtered samples to a new CSV.
items.2: Confirm replacement of the current table. Save the original CSV first if needed.

science.signals.overview: Signal analysis. Arrows/Enter choose; F5/Esc returns one level.

items.0: Require exactly 8,16,32,64 or128 finite Y samples, uniformly sampled at the declared rate. No rows are silently dropped.
items.1: Set sample rate, window and mean removal.
items.2: Check increasing uniform X spacing and convert declared X time units to seconds. Empty units mean seconds for this action.
items.3: Open bounded time-domain filters using the same sample rate.
items.4: After confirmation, create a 16 Hz unit-amplitude sine sampled at 128 Hz for 32 rows.
items.5: Declare data units; this does not rescale existing CSV magnitudes.
items.6: Save settings or read FFT/filter scaling and limitations.

research.home.overview: Advanced studies keep their own inputs, two data tables and matrix. Save them together as a .study document. Nothing recalculates until you request it.

items.0: Implicit curves, contour maps and local optimization inside rectangular bounds.
items.1: QR, SVD, pseudoinverse, symmetric eigenvectors and least squares for square matrices up to 6 by 6.
items.2: One-sided limits, Taylor approximations, finite sums/products and selected improper integrals.
items.3: Additional distributions, exact binomial tests, weighted fits, Welch tests and correlated uncertainty.
items.4: Convolution, correlation, power spectra and low-order continuous-time transfer functions.
items.5: Capture data, inspect both saved tables and send a table to the existing statistics workbench.
items.6: Read actual device memory watermarks and benchmark expression evaluation / PSRAM transfers.
items.7: Read worked examples and the numerical limits before choosing a calculation.

research.files.overview: A study contains equations, both data tables, units, the numerical matrix, transfer coefficients, measurement inputs and settings. Results remain transient.

items.0: Write a named .study under /db48x/studies using temporary-file replacement and backup recovery.
items.1: Validate the whole file before replacing the current study. Opening never runs its equations.
items.2: Change the saved title and notes. These do not affect calculations.
items.3: Read how to capture data, save, reopen and explicitly rerun a study.

research.implicit.overview: Equation entry accepts left=right or a field F(X,Y). An equation is plotted as its left-minus-right residual; level zero is its solution set.

items.0: Edit the equation or scalar field. Try X^2+Y^2=25 for a circle.
items.1: Set the visible X/Y window. This does not change optimization bounds.
items.2: Choose one to three residual/field levels; level zero solves an entered equation.
items.3: Draw bounded marching-square contours in the unified native graph. Undefined samples leave holes.
items.4: Enter a separate objective F(X,Y) for optimization.
items.5: Set rectangular search bounds and the initial point; values are clamped into the box when solving.
items.6: Choose a local numerical minimum or maximum. No global optimum is promised.
items.7: Save/open the connected study or read help.

research.optimize.overview: Pattern search is limited to 400 iterations and 4096 evaluations. Stopping means the search step became small, not a proof of a global optimum.

items.0: Search for a local minimum inside the configured X/Y box.
items.1: Search for a local maximum inside the configured X/Y box.

research.contour_levels.overview: Select which plotted level is highlighted. This changes the active level, not the equation or crosshair position.

items.0: Select contour level one.
items.1: Select contour level two, if enabled.
items.2: Select contour level three, if enabled.

research.linear.overview: Study matrices are real, numerical and dimensionless, with 1..6 rows and columns. Original Matrix workbench arithmetic remains available for exact and unit-bearing calculations.

items.0: Copy the current square matrix A after confirmation. Fractions are evaluated numerically; physical units are rejected.
items.1: Show Q and R with A=QR; rank-deficient columns are reported.
items.2: Show singular values and the U,V factors of A=U diag(s) V^T.
items.3: Show the pseudoinverse, numerical rank and condition diagnostic.
items.4: Compute eigenvalues/vectors for a real symmetric matrix. General nonsymmetric eigenvectors are outside this tool.
items.5: Use the first N Y values of study table B as b; solve with the SVD pseudoinverse.
items.6: Save/open the study or read help.

research.qr.overview: QR uses two orthogonalization passes. Rank-deficient columns are retained as zeros; use SVD for rank and a pseudoinverse.

items.0: View/copy Q; its nonzero columns are orthonormal.
items.1: View/copy upper-triangular R.

research.svd.overview: A=U diag(s) V^T. Singular values <= largest*1e-12 are treated as zero for rank and pseudoinverse. Large condition numbers indicate sensitivity.

items.0: View/copy singular values, numerical rank and condition.
items.1: View/copy U, including an orthonormal completion for zero singular values.
items.2: View/copy V; use its transpose in the reconstruction.

research.eigen.overview: This numerical eigensolver accepts real symmetric matrices only. Eigenvector signs are arbitrary and repeated eigenvalues need not have a unique basis.

items.0: View/copy eigenvalues in the same order as the vector columns.
items.1: View/copy eigenvectors; each column corresponds to one listed eigenvalue.

research.calculus.overview: These guided tools use radians and preserve stored calculator variables. A numerical limit or refinement test is not a symbolic proof.

items.0: Edit the real scalar function F(X).
items.1: Set the limit/expansion point, finite sequence bounds and Taylor degree.
items.2: Estimate a left, right or two-sided finite limit. Divergent/unresolved sequences fail.
items.3: Use supported symbolic derivatives, evaluated numerically, to form a local Taylor approximation through degree four.
items.4: Sum or multiply up to 1000 real numerical terms at integer X.
items.5: Estimate a selected infinite-interval integral by transformed, bounded midpoint refinement.
items.6: Save/open the study or read help.

research.limit.overview: Nearby samples must stabilize. Oscillatory functions or behavior between samples can evade this numerical test.

items.0: Require the sampled left/right sequences to agree.
items.1: Approach the configured point from smaller X.
items.2: Approach the configured point from larger X.

research.sum.overview: First/last indices are inclusive integers, within +/-1e6, with at most 1000 terms. Results are numerical; RPL summation/product commands remain separate.

items.0: Add F(X) over the integer range.
items.1: Multiply F(X) over the integer range.

research.integral.overview: Uses transformed midpoint refinement with at most 4064 evaluations. A small refinement change is not a rigorous error bound or proof of convergence.

items.0: Integrate from the configured first bound to positive infinity.
items.1: Integrate from negative infinity to the configured first bound.
items.2: Integrate over the whole real line; the finite bounds are unused.

research.taylor.overview: Coefficients are evaluated symbolic derivatives divided by k!. The polynomial is local; no remainder bound is inferred.

items.0: View/copy coefficients in ascending powers of (X-X0).
items.1: Plot the approximation across X0 +/- 1 using the native graph.

research.statistics.overview: Study tables A/B hold independent snapshots. Check their units before combining samples. Confidence intervals depend on the stated statistical assumptions.

items.0: Choose uniform, exponential, Student t or chi-square parameters.
items.1: Evaluate a cumulative probability, inverse percentile or CDF plot.
items.2: Run a two-sided probability-ordering binomial test for up to 200 trials.
items.3: Fit a weighted line/quadratic to table A; estimate common residual variance and Student t coefficient intervals.
items.4: Compare mean Y of independent tables A and B without assuming equal variances.
items.5: Set correlated measurements and run first-order or seeded Gaussian Monte Carlo propagation.
items.6: Save/open the study or read help.

research.distribution.overview: These are additional numerical distributions; the existing normal, binomial and Poisson workbench is unchanged.

items.0: Uniform between increasing a and b.
items.1: Exponential with positive rate a.
items.2: Student t with positive degrees of freedom a.
items.3: Chi-square with positive degrees of freedom a.

research.distribution_actions.overview: CDF means P(X <= point). A percentile p must be strictly between 0 and 1.

items.0: Evaluate the cumulative probability at the configured point X.
items.1: Find a numerical inverse CDF at p after bracketing.
items.2: Plot a representative CDF interval in the native engine.

research.uncertainty.overview: Measurements follow the supplied correlated Gaussian model for Monte Carlo. First-order propagation needs a smooth function. Neither result automatically establishes a confidence interval.

items.0: Edit F(A,B,C).
items.1: Enter unit declarations, nominal values and nonnegative standard uncertainties for A,B,C, then output units.
items.2: Enter correlations AB,AC,BC. The matrix must be positive definite; perfect correlations are rejected.
items.3: Compute the nominal value and correlated first-order standard uncertainty.
items.4: Set 128..2048 draws and a nonzero 32-bit seed for repeatable simulation.
items.5: Simulate correlated Gaussian inputs. Invalid-domain draws stop the run rather than being discarded.
items.6: Save/open the study or read help.

research.signals.overview: Y observations are treated as uniform samples at the declared rate. Continuous-time transfer functions use descending powers of Laplace s, up to degree three.

items.0: Set positive sample rate, response duration and Bode frequency bounds.
items.1: Compute the complete discrete convolution or cross-correlation when output length is <=128.
items.2: Estimate a one-sided Welch PSD with Hann windows, mean removal and 50% overlap.
items.3: Edit numerator and denominator coefficients, highest power first.
items.4: Calculate finite numerator/denominator roots.
items.5: Plot gain in dB or phase in degrees against log10(frequency in Hz).
items.6: Integrate a unit step/impulse response for a strictly proper transfer function.
items.7: Save/open the study or read help.

research.convolution.overview: The complete output must fit 128 rows. X is index/sample_rate (or lag/sample_rate). No input or output tail is silently discarded.

items.0: Compute sum A[i]*B[n-i], without a sample-time multiplier.
items.1: Compute sum A[i]*B[i+lag] over valid overlapping indices, without normalization.

research.psd.overview: Uses 64-sample segments when possible, otherwise 32; Hann window, mean removal and 50% overlap. PSD units are input Y squared per Hz.

items.0: Plot one-sided power per hertz. This differs from the port 24 peak-amplitude FFT.
items.1: Export frequency/PSD observations as CSV; preserve the unit convention when using them elsewhere.

research.poles.overview: Roots are in the continuous-time Laplace s-plane (1/s). Numerical roots can fail; right-half-plane poles imply instability.

items.0: Find denominator roots, retaining multiplicity.
items.1: Find finite numerator roots; a constant numerator has none.

research.bode.overview: The horizontal graph coordinate is log10(frequency in Hz): X=3 means 1000 Hz. Phase uses the principal angle; wrapping is not unwrapped.

items.0: Plot 20*log10(abs(H(j*2*pi*f))).
items.1: Plot the principal phase of H(j*2*pi*f) in degrees.

research.response.overview: Strictly proper functions only: numerator degree must be smaller than denominator degree. Numerical response is not a stability proof; fast/stiff dynamics may be unresolved.

items.0: Apply a unit step at t=0 with zero initial state.
items.1: Apply a unit impulse at t=0; the initial state accounts for its jump.

research.documents.overview: Tables and inputs are copied, not live references. Reopening a study runs nothing; choose a calculation explicitly to rerun it.

items.0: Copy current Data / statistics observations into study A after confirmation.
items.1: Copy current observations into study B after confirmation.
items.2: Inspect/plot study A.
items.3: Inspect/plot study B.
items.4: Replace current Data / statistics observations with A after confirmation.
items.5: Replace current observations with B after confirmation.
items.6: Save/open the self-contained study, or edit its title and notes.
items.7: Read the complete capture/save/reopen/rerun workflow.
